title: Mind the Gap (In your Agent Observability) — Amy Boyd & Nitya Narasimhan, Microsoft
talk_summary: A Microsoft Foundry workshop on agent observability: tracing (OpenTelemetry-based), built-in quality/safety/agentic evaluators, trace-linked evaluations, red teaming, and an early-preview 'observe' coding-agent skill that auto-generates eval datasets, runs batch evals, optimizes prompts, versions and rolls back agents. Most content is product-specific to Foundry, but the underlying loop (trace-linked evals, auto-generated eval sets, versioned prompt optimization with regression checks) is portable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Attach eval scores to the specific trace/step that produced them, so a failing metric points directly at the agent step (e.g. a tool call that stopped firing) rather than requiring a separate debugging pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: trace linked evaluations are where it's at ... you can look at the emails and figure out what part of the trace

takeaways.technique: Auto-generated eval datasets from agent instructions
takeaways.what_they_do: When no eval set exists, a coding agent reads the agent's instructions/endpoint and synthesizes a starter eval dataset, runs a baseline batch eval, then reports failures with reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You don't have an eval data set ... I know what you're trying to do because you've shown me the instructions. I'm going to start building this out

takeaways.technique: Prompt-optimizer loop with versioning and rollback
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent analyzes eval failures, rewrites the prompt, bumps a version, re-runs the same batch evals, compares before/after, and rolls back to the best-scoring version if it regresses.
takeaways.numbers: improved by one issue; best version was version five of ten tried

takeaways.technique: Specialist agents + declarative workflow with per-agent traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Split a monolithic agent into specialist agents (flight/hotel/car) orchestrated by a declarative YAML workflow, so traces show which sub-agent underperforms and only that one gets optimized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're able to see which of these agents is underperforming ... and then flip out only the agents that you need to optimize

takeaways.technique: Automated red teaming of agent actions
takeaways.what_they_do: A second AI attacks the agent across risk categories and attack strategies (leetspeak, crescendo) including 'prohibited actions' — a taxonomy of actions the agent must never take.

When switching to a cheaper model, immediately run the eval suite to check for regression, and inspect traces to see which tool calls got slower/expensive (e.g. web search) and replace with cached data.
